summary: A pasture or fat grazing place. The Psalm uses the plural for the fat of pasture, which vanishes like smoke. In Genesis 13:10, כִּכָּר designates the plain along the Jordan. Lot surveys the whole district and sees that it is well watered.

senses.definition: The wicked pass away like the fat of pasture, disappearing like smoke.
A tract of level land along a river.

evidence.note: The construct phrase כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן names the land along the Jordan that Lot sees, and כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה describes the entire tract as well watered.

note:
The source brief files k.cx.af after כפש, but the consecutive rootless heading and unrelated pasture sense make כר the safer root. Verify against the underlying BDB index.

Root (2026-11-21): Filed under the geminate root כרר with כִּכָּר (kkikkaar), the root of כַּר 'he-lamb' as well; how 'pasture' (Isa 30:23, Psa 65:14) relates to turning or roundness is not clear.

Added 2026-11-21: כִּכָּר, from its former one-word entry. Filed under the geminate root כרר 'turn round': כִּכָּר stands for *kirkar 'a round' (district, loaf, talent), as its plural כִּכְּרִין and כִּרְכָּרוֹת (Isa 66:20) show, and the verb מְכַרְכֵּר 'whirling' (2Sa 6:14, 16) and Arabic كَرَّ 'turn back, return' (Lane p. 2600) belong with it. כַּר (kkar) goes under the same root.

Its former note: The geographic use is clear in this verse. Its semantic connection to כרר is uncertain.
